label: bug
file: none

Thanks for the detailed report. The "Malformed row" message itself only lives in src/i18n/en.json as a string, not in the parsing logic, so the search didn't turn up the actual CSV-parsing code path that raises errors.rowShape.

Given the timing (it started right after finance switched to a new Windows-based accounting export tool) and that the file opens fine in a spreadsheet, this strongly points to a format change in the exported CSV rather than a change on Ledgerline's side — most likely one of:
- a UTF-8 byte-order-mark (BOM) at the start of the file that gets attached to the header's first column name, making the header appear to have a mismatched/garbled first column,
- CRLF vs LF line-ending differences from the new tool confusing the row splitter, or
- a delimiter change (e.g. semicolon instead of comma) that spreadsheets auto-detect but our parser does not.

Could you attach one of the failing files (or just its first two lines) so we can confirm which of these it is and fix the importer to tolerate it? In the meantime, re-saving the export as plain UTF-8 CSV (no BOM) with comma delimiters from the spreadsheet app may work around it.
